evaluations.label: A
errors: "to accommodate approximately 15 to 18 people": the transcript says 15 people and 18 positions, not 15 to 18 people.

"Action Items: (none)": the transcript has clear assignments (Andre to check room separation, four desks in a 3P room, and Gisella with the school admin; Susan to ask Maggie and Pierrette; everyone to bring a proposal; meeting next Tuesday 2 pm).
"negotiation with other groups in the building": the other group is a second committee drafting an alternative allocation, not other groups in the building competing for the space.
"Members were tasked with consulting colleagues, such as Maggie and Pierrette": Susan specifically volunteered to ask Maggie and Pierrette; it was not a task given to all members.
Speakers are labeled Speaker 1 to Speaker 4 with no mapping to Andre, Martin, Susan, David even though the names are used in the transcript, so attributions cannot be checked by a reader.
strengths: Core space facts are right: sixth floor, 1P/2P/3P rooms, furniture per person, photocopier/fax/printer, 15 people vs 18 slots including the reading room, Martin and David part-time.
The Unresolved Questions section correctly lists the open items: room partitioning, four in a 3P room, lounge purpose, professors wanting their own offices.
Next meeting Tuesday 2:00 PM is correct.
weaknesses: Explicitly reports no action items, which is the single biggest failure for someone who missed the meeting.

Omits Susan's and Martin's stated positions by name, the 16-slots-for-15 arithmetic, the zero-growth concern, the smoking rule, the four-desk check, the Gisella-with-school-admin idea, and the fixed-rooms/free-arrangement point.
Speaker numbers instead of names make the notes hard to act on; the summary and outline repeat each other.

evaluations.label: B
errors: "Susan and Martin both raised concerns about sharing offices": Martin said he has nothing against sharing and did it before; his only caveat was his phone calls (the sub-bullet gets this right).
"The group discussed meeting the following Tuesday afternoon, around 2 p.m.": this was agreed, not just discussed.
Name spelled Andrei (transcript: Andre); minor.
strengths: Almost every statement checks out against the transcript, with correct attributions: Martin on zero growth and meeting rooms, Susan on splitting rooms and rectorate confidentiality, Martin on budget confidentiality, Susan volunteering to ask Maggie and Pierrette.
Correctly frames the meeting as constraint-gathering with no layout decided, and that room count is fixed while assignments are open.
Gisella options (1P room, or 2P room with the second desk unresolved) are stated correctly.
Timestamps make claims easy to verify.
weaknesses: Action items list only two of Andre's and Susan's commitments; it omits Andre checking four desks in a 3P room, Andre asking about placing Gisella with the school admin, every attendee bringing a sketch/proposal, and the Tuesday 2 pm meeting as a dated next step.
Misses David's stated preference to share with an assistant, the Gisella-with-school-admin option, the coffee/cafeteria facts, and that professors in other faculties have their own offices.
Summary header and first bullets repeat the same point three times.

evaluations.label: C
errors: Action item "Distribute documents of the new office configuration to all participants" assigned to Andrei: the documents were handed out during the meeting; this is not a follow-up task.
Action item "Follow up with absent team members (Maggie, Pierrette)" assigned to Andrei: Susan explicitly took this ("Okay, I'll ask Maggie and Pierrette").

"Coffee and vending machines available within the building, but no dedicated cafeteria" contradicts the transcript (Susan: the cafeteria is downstairs, closes at five) and the notes' own next bullet about cafeterias closing at 5 PM.
"Management recognizes this as a priority due to previously lengthy discussions on its value": not said; Martin only joked that Susan should valorize the time spent discussing the room.

"merge proposals with another group before next Tuesday's review meeting": Andre said the merge happens when the other group's proposal is available, after building one coherent proposal; not before Tuesday.
"Growth is effectively zero unless visitors or temporary staff share existing desks": the 'unless' clause is invented; desk sharing was explicitly rejected.

"The team expects to manage this through proposals and iterative feedback rather than direct surveys": Martin also proposed asking everyone for their own place, so 'rather than direct surveys' is not supported.
"The session will focus on refining the plan rather than final decisions": Andre said the next meeting should try to come up with one solution.
"Smoking is allowed only outside, even on balconies" is garbled; the transcript says smoking is allowed on the balcony.
"Lounge Priority: A lounge/reading room is key": Susan questioned whether it was needed at all; the transcript shows demand plus an open debate, not an agreed priority.
strengths: Broadest coverage of the four: includes the four-desks-in-a-3P-room check, the Gisella-with-school-admin idea, the one-free-slot visitor limit, the smoking rule, coffee/vending machines, and the other group's parallel proposal.
Correctly captures the room count being fixed with all permutations open, the move away from project grouping, and the admin room options.
Lists the three real Andre follow-ups (separation, four desks, admin placement) and the all-participants proposal task.
weaknesses: Very long and repetitive (the lounge, growth, visitors and room-splitting each appear three or four times), which buries the few things a reader must act on.
Names are almost entirely stripped out ("some staff", "others", "the team"), so who holds which position is lost; Susan's and Martin's clear stances are not attributable.
The action item list mixes real commitments with invented ones and misassigns Maggie/Pierrette to Andrei, which is exactly where a reader would rely on the notes.

evaluations.label: D
errors: "Majority lean toward a mixed-use room": Martin said some people including himself want a mixed room and that the discussion is still open with no decision; no majority was established.
"Strong support for a dedicated lounge/reading room": Andre said quite a lot of people expressed the need, but Susan asked whether it was needed at all; 'strong support' overstates.
"Shared space with another group": the other group is a second committee producing an alternative allocation for the same ISSCO rooms, not a group sharing the space.

"give her a 2P room with a visitor slot": the option was raised, but Martin and Susan then said putting a senior visitor in the admin office is not realistic (only an exchange student or intern); the notes drop that caveat.
Next steps carry no owners, although the transcript assigns separation, four-desk and admin checks to Andre and the Maggie/Pierrette ask to Susan.
strengths: All six next steps match the transcript: room separation, four desks in a 3P room, Gisella with the school admin, Maggie and Pierrette preferences, each attendee bringing a sketch, and next Tuesday 2 pm after the morning MDM meeting at Unimail.

Positions are named and correct: Susan prefers her own office (phone calls, rectorate confidentiality), Martin open to sharing but on the phone a lot, project grouping dropped, own desk for everyone, smoking no longer a constraint, Andre and Agnes negotiate with the other group.
Gets the key numbers right: 15 people, ~18 positions counting the reading room, 16 slots for 15 if a 2P room becomes the lounge, zero growth margin; also the correct coffee/cafeteria facts.
Compact and scannable; a reader who missed the meeting can act on it.
weaknesses: Next steps are not assigned to people, so a reader does not know Andre owns three of them and Susan one.

Omits David's preference to share with an assistant, Martin's budget-confidentiality point, Martin's remark that people will not state who they refuse to sit with, and that this meeting's goal was constraints only.
A couple of soft overstatements (majority, strong support) where the transcript shows an open debate.

rationale: D is the most useful and the only set whose next-steps list matches every commitment in the transcript, with named positions and correct numbers; its faults are missing owners and two overstatements about the lounge debate. B is the most accurate statement by statement, with correct attributions and timestamps, but its action list captures only two of the six follow-ups and it omits several points, so it ranks second. C covers the most ground but is bloated, strips out names, contradicts itself on the cafeteria, and its action items include an invented task and misassign the Maggie/Pierrette ask to Andrei instead of Susan, so it ranks third. A reports no action items at all, uses unresolved speaker numbers instead of the names available in the transcript, and misses the main follow-ups, so it ranks last despite few outright factual errors.
